mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (or Certificate of Registration of Foreign-Invested Partnership)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: notarize if private document, or authenticate the official registry document directly, then obtain an Apostille certificate from the High Court of Hong Kong for a state party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention. Consular Legalization path (mutually exclusive alternative, for non-member states): notarize/authenticate, then legalize at the consulate or embassy of the destination state in Hong Kong or Beijing. Never chain the two paths.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Current Status)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: authentication by the High Court of Hong Kong and issuance of an Apostille for Hague Convention states. Consular Legalization path: authentication by the High Court followed by consular legalization at the destination state's consulate in Hong Kong. Use either path exclusively; do not combine sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney of the General Partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: General partner of the Foreign-Invested Partnership, notarized by a Hong Kong Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: notarization by a Hong Kong Notary Public, then Apostille from the High Court of Hong Kong. Consular Legalization path: notarization by a Hong Kong Notary Public, then authentication by the High Court, then legalization by the destination state's consulate in Hong Kong. These paths are mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Partnership Agreement (constitutional instrument)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: All partners executing the agreement under Hong Kong law, notarized by a Hong Kong Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: notarize the partnership agreement and obtain an Apostille from the High Court of Hong Kong for Apostille Convention jurisdictions. Consular Legalization path: notarize, authenticate at the High Court, and present to the destination state's consulate in Hong Kong for legalization. Never chain Apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank in Hong Kong (e.g., HSBC, Standard Chartered, Bank of China (Hong Kong))
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: the bank's authorized officer must sign, the signature is notarized by a Hong Kong Notary Public, and the High Court of Hong Kong issues an Apostille. Consular Legalization path: notarize the bank officer's signature, authenticate at the High Court, then legalize at the destination state's consulate in Hong Kong. The two authentication paths are parallel and exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Business Registration Office, Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: the official certificate is authenticated by the High Court of Hong Kong, which then issues an Apostille for Apostille Convention states. Consular Legalization path: the certificate is authenticated by the High Court and legalized by the destination state's consulate in Hong Kong. Do not use both processes.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every partner, general partner, authorized representative, and beneficial owner holding at least 25% of the Foreign-Invested Partnership must be screened before incorporation and on a rolling basis against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and Non-SDN sanction lists, UK HM Treasury sanctions, EU restrictive measures, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's specified persons and terrorist financing list under Cap. 615, and PRC domestic terrorist designations. PEP screening must cover immediate family, close associates, source of funds, source of wealth, and the full corporate ownership chain. Adverse hits trigger enhanced due diligence and may require rejection or regulatory referral. All screening results must be documented, retained for at least five years, and updated at least quarterly for this EdTech subscription engagement.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Hong Kong Companies Registry e-Registry and Cyber Search Centre (ICRIS) with the Business Registration Office (BRO) of the Inland Revenue Department through the One-Stop Company and Business Registration Service
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: English names must use Latin characters; Chinese names must be in Traditional Chinese characters only; simplified Chinese is not acceptable for statutory registration. If both English and Chinese names are registered, the Chinese name may be a phonetic transliteration or a semantic translation of the English name, but it must not be offensive, misleading, or falsely imply government patronage. The four-tier naming convention requires: (1) uniqueness against the statutory register; (2) no confusing resemblance to an existing name; (3) no prohibited terms absent prior ministerial consent; and (4) no misleading indication of limited liability status for a partnership.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: An approved name reservation is valid for 30 days and may be extended online through the Companies Registry e-Registry for one additional 30-day period before expiry, subject to payment of the prescribed extension fee and confirmation that the name remains available. If the name is rejected, the applicant should request written reasons from the Registrar. The applicant may submit a revised name free of charge within 14 days. If the applicant disputes the rejection, a formal appeal must be filed with the Companies Registry Review Committee within 21 days, including the rejection notice, statutory declaration, and written submissions. The Committee will decide within 15 working days. Further recourse is by way of judicial review in the Court of First Instance of the Hong Kong High Court.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: In Hong Kong, a virtual office address or commercial mailbox may be accepted by the Companies Registry and the Business Registration Office for basic registration purposes. However, the Inland Revenue Department and licensed banks generally reject a virtual office for an EdTech subscription entity without further commercial substance. The IRD may challenge territorial-source profit claims and the HKMA's AML expectations require banks to verify a physical place of business and to reject high-risk or no-substance entities. Because this entity is a Foreign-Invested Partnership using app-store payment rails, a serviced office with a physical lease, meeting rooms, named signage, local correspondence handling, and accounting records is strongly recommended. A bare mailbox will likely be deemed insufficient and may validate a refusal of bank account opening or an IRD inspection.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced on-site inspections by Inland Revenue Department field audit officers and Companies Registry examiners are possible though infrequent for a low-risk EdTech subscription partnership. Checklist for inspection readiness: (1) valid lease or serviced-office agreement at the registered address; (2) name signage at the premises; (3) utility bills or service bills in the entity's name; (4) attendance or staffing records; (5) statutory and accounting records maintained at the registered address; (6) transactional records for subscription sales; (7) evidence of local management or business substance. Quantified risk: below 5% per annum for a physical office with adequate substance; approximately 15% per annum for a virtual office with a local agent but no lease; above 40% per annum for a virtual office with no local staffing and opaque UBO documentation.

incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form LP-1 under the Limited Partnership Ordinance (Cap. 37); Form IR(BR)1A under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Hong Kong has no minimum paid-up capital for a Foreign-Invested Partnership. A nominal contribution of HK$1 may be declared in the partnership agreement. Capital may be held in an ordinary operating account; no blocked escrow or capital escrow account is prescribed by the Companies Registry or the Business Registration Office.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF THE FOREIGN-INVESTED PARTNERSHIP - ADOPTED IN WRITING BY THE GENERAL PARTNER ON THE ____ DAY OF ________, 20____. WHEREAS the Foreign-Invested Partnership (FIP) has been organized as a limited partnership under the laws of Hong Kong, with pass-through taxation status; and WHEREAS the partners have agreed upon the initial subscribed capital, business objects, and governance provisions contained in the executed partnership agreement; and WHEREAS the FIP will engage in ISIC 6201 computer programming activities, namely interactive language education and automated tutoring software, distributed through Apple IAP and Google Play Billing; and WHEREAS the Companies Registry and the Business Registration Office require the FIP to maintain a registered office, a statutory responsible person, and authorized officers for the conduct of banking and payment operations. NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that: (1) The subscribed capital commitments set forth in Schedule I of the partnership agreement are ratified. There is no minimum paid-up capital under Hong Kong law; no blocked escrow account is required. The General Partner is empowered to make capital calls and to open and maintain an operating account for the receipt and disbursement of funds. (2) The General Partner is authorized to open, close, and operate bank accounts in the name of the FIP, to sign account opening forms, signature cards, electronic banking mandates, standing instructions, and settlement agreements with Apple, Google, and payment aggregators. (3) The registered office of the FIP shall be maintained at the address filed with the Companies Registry, and the General Partner may appoint a registered agent and may change the office upon filing the requisite notice. (4) The following statutory officers are appointed and authorized: [full name] as General Partner and Chief Governance Officer; [full name] as AML Compliance Officer; [full name] as Partnership Secretary; and [full name] as Responsible Person for Business Registration. (5) The officers are directed to prepare and file the Business Registration Certificate application, annual exemption statement, and all tax forms, and to engage a licensed Hong Kong Certified Public Accountant to prepare accounts and tax computations. (6) All deeds, contracts, online agreements, and purchase orders may be executed by any one authorized officer. This resolution is effective upon adoption and shall continue until revoked in writing. IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have executed this resolution as a single instrument.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name availability search and preliminary filing preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, Hong Kong SAR - One-Stop Integrated e-Platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name search through the official e-Platform of the Companies Registry and Business Registration Office before any execution. The applicant must verify that the proposed English name and Chinese name are not identical to an existing registered company or limited partnership and that the name is not misleading or prohibited. If the name uses sensitive words such as bank, trust, insurance, or education, a written consent from the relevant licensing authority must be attached. File the prescribed name-check application electronically, pay the applicable name-search fee, and preserve the generated receipt. The name is not a separate reservation for partnerships; availability is confirmed when the registration application is accepted. A lawful formation requires that the name exactly match the partnership agreement, constitution, and all banking KYC documents.
required_dossiers: Proposed English name
Proposed Chinese name if used
Name search report
Consent letter for restricted or sensitive words if applicable
Applicant and general partner identification documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name application or pre-filing is suspended, revise the name to a sufficiently distinct alternative and re-apply. A written response to the Registrar's query must be submitted within 21 days. An oral hearing may be requested for contested names, and evidence of business distinctiveness may cure an objection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and registration of the partnership agreement and Form LP-1
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, Hong Kong SAR - Partnership Registration Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the partnership agreement and all constituent documents before any statutory filing. The General Partner must circulate the agreement to each limited partner for execution and counter-execution. The agreement must state the firm name, General Partner, limited partners, capital commitments, profit-sharing ratios, dissolution events, arbitration or alternative dispute resolution clauses, governing law, and bank account mandates. Each foreign partner must deliver a notarized power of attorney or apostilled corporate resolution if the partner is a body corporate. If a partner cannot sign in Hong Kong, the signature may be witnessed by an authorized officer of the partnership agent; however, the Companies Registry may require a certified copy. After execution, upload the signed partnership agreement and Form LP-1 to the Companies Registry e-Platform, or file at the physical counter with the prescribed fee.
required_dossiers: Executed partnership agreement with capital schedule
Form LP-1 signed by the General Partner
Notarized or apostilled power of attorney for foreign corporate partners
Certified true copy of the General Partner's constitutional documents if corporate
Identity and address proof of each partner
Registered office address proof
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar rejects or marks the application as irregular, amend the partnership agreement or Form LP-1 and resubmit within 14 days. Notify all partners, pay any re-filing fee, and obtain the corrected certificate. A solicitor's affirmation may cure defective signatures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business registration with the Business Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Business Registration Office, Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon issuance of the partnership registration certificate, file the business registration application with the Business Registration Office, entering the exact name, nature of business, registered address, date of commencement, and identification of the General Partner and the Responsible Person. For the EdTech subscription business, describe the principal activity as computer programming, software publishing, and online education, using ISIC 6201 where requested. Pay the annual business registration fee and the levy by e-Cheque, PPS, or online. The Business Registration Certificate is an absolute condition precedent to operating, invoicing subscribers, and onboarding payment intermediaries. The business registration number must be shown on all invoices, correspondence, and e-commerce portals. Submit a copy to the bank and to Apple IAP and Google Play Billing during merchant verification. If the business address is not an industrial plot, no industrial environmental impact assessment is required.
required_dossiers: Completed Form IR(BR)1A
Partnership registration certificate from the Companies Registry
Identity documents of the General Partner and Responsible Person
Lease or documentary proof of the registered office address
Declaration of business activities and nature of digital services
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Inland Revenue Department raises an objection to the business registration or the business description, file a written representation within 14 days with amended Form IR(BR)1A and supporting contracts. If penalties are assessed, apply for remission in writing before the due date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Completion of post-formation governance, bank account opening, and AML/KYC onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed banks in Hong Kong under Hong Kong Monetary Authority AML/CFT guidelines; Companies Registry for record filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the post-formation governance obligations, including opening the operating bank account, compiling the partnership register, and appointing the AML and compliance officers. The General Partner must pass a banking mandate resolution and provide specimen signatures to a licensed bank under the HKMA. The bank will request beneficial ownership, source of funds, proof of business activity, transaction flow charts, and the payment processor agreements. The General Partner must also file the annual business registration renewal and any changes of the registered office with the Companies Registry within the statutory period. Maintain the register of partners and any significant controllers at the registered office. For payment providers, upload the legal entity formation documents, business registration certificate, bank confirmation letter, and the board resolution. Allow five business days for statutory filings and bank opening or seven days if the bank requests further compliance documents.
required_dossiers: Banking mandate resolution
Specimen signature cards
Beneficial ownership declaration
Source of funds statement
Business registration certificate and partnership registration certificate
Apple IAP and Google Play Billing merchant application forms
AML compliance officer appointment letter
Partnership register and significant controllers register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or payment processor returns a refusal or query, provide a legal opinion issued by a Hong Kong solicitor and a comprehensive ownership and source-of-funds declaration. Where permissible, transfer the application to another licensed bank or contact the HKMA mediation mechanism for business account access.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China, administered through the local competent tax bureau of the FIP's registration address; electronic registration, filings, and tax administration are performed through the Integrated Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax) national portal of the STA.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Register the Foreign-Invested Partnership (FIP) with the local office of the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and obtain the business license reflecting the partnership and foreign investment status. Step 2: Under China's multi-license integration system, the tax registration is completed automatically upon market registration, and the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC) issued by the SAMR functions as the FIP's Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN). Step 3: Activate the TIN and tax filing profile in the e-Tax portal, set up bank account records, legal representative or delegated tax agent credentials, and taxpayer type. Step 4: File the taxpayer status election for VAT purposes: either small-scale taxpayer or general VAT taxpayer, depending on expected annual taxable sales. Step 5: For cross-border services, complete the Cross-Border Taxable Services Tax Exemption/Zero-Rating Filing with the competent tax authority before the first zero-rated export transaction. Step 6: Register each non-resident partner in the withholding tax register and record the partner's foreign tax identification number and tax residence documentation, including a Hong Kong Tax Resident Certificate where relief under the Mainland and Hong Kong Double Tax Arrangement is sought.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible (the FIP is not an entity-level Enterprise Income Tax taxpayer; each partner is taxed on its allocable share of PRC-source income under PRC partnership tax transparency rules, while the FIP is independently registered as a VAT taxpayer for indirect tax purposes).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for income tax classification: PRC law statutor

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) under the People's Bank of China (PBOC), with SAFE provincial branches and designated domestic banks acting as the operational enforcement and verification channel
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Chinese mainland operates a managed floating exchange-rate regime in which current account transactions are generally freely convertible once a bank has performed genuine trade background verification, while capital account transactions remain strictly controlled and require prior registration, approval, and bank-level compliance review. For a Foreign-Invested Partnership (FIP) in China, foreign limited partners injecting equity capital must first complete foreign direct investment (FDI) information registration with SAFE or through the receiving bank's digital SAFE portal. The resulting registered capital is held in a foreign exchange capital account and can be settled into RMB only for permitted business expenditures, not for onward investment or speculative use. Profit remittances to non-resident partners are current account items but require a verifiable audited financial statement, a tax payment or tax exemption certificate, board or all-partner resolution, proof of paid-in capital, and confirmation that the distribution arises from genuinely earned operating profits. Convertibility of the current account is real but administratively conditional, and the bank or SAFE may freeze settlement if the EdTech subscription revenue flow appears inconsistent with the declared commercial scope. Overall, CNY is convertible for trade and service receipts, but capital account movement is gated by SAFE registrations and cannot be replaced by offshore fintech rails without substantial penalty and compliance risk.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export and cross-border service revenue receipts must be repatriated into China through a designated domestic bank and reported under SAFE's Trade Monitoring System; the statutory conversion model is market-based, meaning there is no fixed mandatory conversion ratio, and the FIP may choose to retain the foreign currency in its current account foreign exchange settlement account or convert it to RMB at the prevailing interbank market rate. Surrender-related verification must occur within the 90-day trade settlement reporting window, supported by valid contracts, invoices, customs data if physical goods are involved, and the bank's electronic verification of the related service delivery for EdTech subscriptions.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low legality and viability for onshore mainland treasury operations. Foreign fintech EMI platforms such as Airwallex, Revolut Business, Currenxie, and similar digital banking providers generally hold financial licenses outside mainland China and are not licensed by the PBOC or SAFE to hold RMB basic deposit accounts, receive FIP registered capital, or clear domestic supplier payments in CNY. Such EMIs may only be used as offshore collection vehicles for foreign app store settlements if the FIP establishes a compliant outbound payment structure under a genuine services arrangement. However, the FIP's statutory capital contributions, SAFE-registered paths, tax filings, and all RMB-denominated operational flows must remain inside a domestic tier-1 bank account. Attempting to run the operating treasury through an offshore EMI will trigger severe AML blockages and capital control violations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a newly formed mainland China FIP, the bank account opening process normally requires the general partner's designated representative, the statutory responsible person, or the authorized financial controller to appear physically at a domestic bank branch to complete the KYC interview, produce original corporate chops, sign bank forms, and undergo photo and biometric verification. Remote consular proxy opening is not generally permitted for a new FIP entity; some banks may accept a notarized power of attorney with Chinese consular legalization, but the bank compliance committee will almost always require at least one physical visit or a bank-arranged video verification under strict branch supervision before issuing operational banking credentials.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inability to establish the full beneficial ownership chain for multiple non-resident limited partners, where partner ownership is in percentages that create perceived layering or nominee-ownership patterns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the notarized partnership agreement, certified register of all partners with identity documents, a beneficiary ownership declaration signed by all general and limited partners, an organizational chart showing each direct and indirect owner to final natural persons, a source-of-funds questionnaire for every non-resident partner, and where any partner is a legal person, audited financial statements plus company incorporation certificates with apostille or Chinese consulate legalization

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspected mismatch between declared EdTech software scope and actual incoming payment flows, especially where Apple IAP and Google Play remittances arrive from platform treasury accounts in Ireland, Singapore, or the United States
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver the commercial contracts with Apple and Google, platform payout statements, monthly merchant settlement reports, server/hosting agreements, product transaction logs, privacy and user terms, a detailed narrative of the SaaS revenue recognition methodology, a certified translation of the business license reflecting ISIC 6201 software development and online education services, and if required by the bank, an independent CPA comfort letter mapping platform receipts to specific app sales

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Concern that the FIP lacks minimum capital substance and is being used as a pass-through vehicle rather than an operational EdTech treasury entity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply the SAFE foreign exchange registration certificate for the FIP, bank-inbound USD or HKD remittance tickets from each foreign limited partner, a registered capital verification report issued by a licensed mainland Chinese public accounting firm, a physical or virtual office lease agreement, payroll records, employee social insurance payment certificates, board meeting minutes approving the treasury mandate, and a 12-month cash-flow forecast demonstrating that the capital equals a genuine operational need for product development, language tutoring content, and platform tools

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Red flag generated by unusual round-tripping or split-transaction structuring in which large partner distributions flow out before adequate tax filings are made, particularly to offshore jurisdictions associated with high-risk tax secrecy
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide complete audited financial statements in the same accounting period as the proposed distribution, corporate income tax prepayment and annual filing receipts issued by the mainland tax bureau, profits-tax settlement certificate, a board-approved distribution resolution, equal treatment evidence for all partners, proof that retained earnings are sourced from verified EdTech subscription turnover, and a clear statement of the withholding tax treatment, including treaty relief certificates if applying under the China-HK double tax arrangement, and a notarized undertaking that no proceeds of crime or foreign-exchange violations are embedded in the distributed funds

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital injections from non-resident limited partners must be routed through the SWIFT system by wire into the FIP's dedicated foreign exchange capital account at a SAFE-approved onshore bank. The remittance instruction should use the SWIFT MT103 message and include a purpose code reflecting cross-border FDI capital injection; the receiving bank will verify the SAFE registration information, the beneficiary FIP name, the registered investment amount, and the capital verification requirements. After the capital is credited and the genuine trading background is confirmed, the FIP may either retain the foreign currency or settle it into RMB. A licensed mainland CPA must subsequently issue a capital verification report, and all shareholder loans or supplementary capital injections must also be reported under SAFE cross-border financing rules, ensuring no unauthorized repayment of principal or diversion of settled RMB into prohibited industries such as speculative trading.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For service and trade disbursements, the primary clearing rails are SWIFT MT103 direct transfers for licensing fees, royalty payments, mobile platform service fees, cloud hosting subscriptions, and dividend remittances; commercial letters of credit and documentary collections are appropriate when the FIP purchases physical hardware, office equipment, or educational content devices from suppliers that still rely on trade finance instruments. Every outbound payment must be submitted to the bank with the underlying contract, tax invoice, service completion certificate or customs declaration, withhold tax payment certificate, and the correct domestic bank foreign exchange payment form; payments to connected overseas platform treasury accounts must match the bank's previously approved treasury profile to avoid anti-fragmentation checks.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore FX forward contracts with real trade background and expiry within 12 months for receivables or payables denominated in USD, HKD, or EUR
Onshore FX swaps between CNY and USD or HKD, permitted only when underlying current account transactions or SAFE-authorized capital account exposures are documented

Cross-currency interest-rate swaps or currency swaps approved on a case-by-case basis by the bank and SAFE when the FIP holds a genuine long-term foreign exchange liability or foreign-currency capital structure

Offshore CNH non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permitted for onshore FIPs; such instruments may be used only at the offshore parent level and must never be mixed with the mainland FIP's RMB treasury flows

Options strategies are restricted to safe, premium-paying buyer structures such as purchased USD/CNY put or call options with clear underlying commercial exposure; naked option-writing and structured barrier products are prohibited

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business Registration Certificate renewal – Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department – Business Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the expiry date of the current one-year certificate; renewal may be submitted no earlier than one month before the expiry date (annual anniversary rule)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal within one month attracts a maximum fine of HK$1,000; late renewal beyond one month attracts a maximum fine of HK$5,000. Carrying on business without a valid certificate is a separate continuing offence, and the Inland Revenue Department may institute prosecution, impose an estimated assessment, and ultimately refuse further renewal.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profits Tax Return for partnership (Form BIR52) with tax computation and audited accounts where income threshold is met
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month from the date of issue of the return; when a licensed tax representative is appointed, the Inland Revenue Department may grant extensions of up to three to eight months depending on the partnership's accounting date (for example, a 31 December year end is commonly extended to the following August)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file without reasonable excuse is an offence under Section 80 of the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112), with a maximum fine of HK$10,000 plus a further penalty of three times the tax undercharged; the Inland Revenue Department may also raise an estimated assessment and levy interest on tax attributable to delay.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Limited Partnership Annual Return (Form LRG/1) – Limited Partnerships Ordinance (Cap. 37)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after the anniversary of the date of registration of the limited partnership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late delivery triggers the Companies Registry late filing tariff, generally starting at HK$600 for missing the statutory 42-day deadline by up to three months and rising to HK$1,200 where the default exceeds three months; on conviction, the partnership and the general partner may be fined up to HK$5,000, with an additional daily default fine for continuing non-compliance. Persistent and unexplained default can ultimately result in administrative strike-off from the register of limited partnerships.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An HK limited partnership is not an incorporated company, so no statutory audit is triggered solely by legal form. However, the Inland Revenue Department requires audited financial statements to accompany Profits Tax Return BIR52 where the partnership's annual gross turnover or gross income exceeds HK$2,000,000; for annual gross income of HK$2,000,000 or below, unaudited financial statements and tax computations may be accepted. There is no balance-sheet or headcount audit exemption threshold for partnerships in Hong Kong, but if the same business were operated through an incorporated Hong Kong company, an independent audit would be required under the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) irrespective of size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS) issued by the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants (HKICPA), aligned with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS); eligible private entities may apply HKFRS for Private Entities / the SME Financial Reporting Framework, while tax computations must be adjusted to the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Limited Partnerships Ordinance (Cap. 37), the partnership must notify the Companies Registry within 30 days of any change in the limited partnership's registered particulars, including changes in partner identity, capital contributions, profit-sharing arrangements, the principal place of business, or the partnership's nature of business. The annual return (Form LRG/1) filed within 42 days after the anniversary of registration serves as the annual confirmation of those same particulars. For anti-money-laundering purposes, the general partner and any AML compliance officer must maintain current KYC/CDD records identifying ultimate beneficial owners; Hong Kong does not maintain a public UBO register for limited partnerships, but those records must be readily accessible on-site for the Companies Registry, the HK Police, and other lawful authorities. Any transfer of a partnership interest therefore triggers the 30-day reportable-change window, in addition to the annual return confirmation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members / Limited Partners (including capital contributions, contribution dates, and profit-sharing ratios)
Register of Directors / General Partners (including identity details and business addresses)
Register of Charges or Mortgages (if any security is granted over partnership assets)
Minute Book (recording resolutions of the general partner and management committee decisions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$1,200 – US$3,000 per year (approximately HK$9,360 – HK$23,400) for a registered business address, licensed corporate service provider, and secretarial/agent support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$4,000 – US$10,000 per year for an independent Hong Kong certified public accountant audit of a cross-border EdTech subscription partnership, with an upward adjustment where transfer-pricing documentation or group consolidation support is required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard corporate income tax at partner level; the Foreign-Invested Partnership itself is a pass-through vehicle and does not pay entity-level CIT)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying High and New Technology Enterprise: 15%; Small Low-Profit Enterprise: effective 5% on taxable income up to RMB 3 million; R&D additional deduction: 100% pre-tax deduction of qualifying R&D expenditure; possible 10-year loss carryforward for qualifying high-tech companies but statutory default remains 5 years

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Mainland China Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return (Form A / Form A100000) plus the mandatory partnership pass-through allocation annex and related-party transaction schedule, filed through the State Administration of Taxation Electronic Tax Administration (e-Tax portal)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with quarterly provisional returns due within 15 days after each quarter-end)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Final annual return and settlement due no later than 31 May following the fiscal year-end; quarterly provisional CIT declarations due within 15 days after each quarter-end; withholding tax for non-resident payments is due within 7 days of the obligation arising

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: FIP legal name, unified social credit code, registered address, fiscal year, and the full schedule of resident and non-resident partners with their share ratios.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the non-resident partner schedule even though the FIP is pass-through; declare each partner's tax status under the Mainland-HK DTA and obtain a Hong Kong Tax Residency Certificate where treaty relief is intended.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Covers the 12-month period ended on the statutory tax year-end (31 December) or the short period created by formation, dissolution, or restructuring.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident corporate partner, confirm that the share of FIP income is allocated to the same PRC taxable year and that any treaty claim applies to the exact year-end covered.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All China-sourced EdTech subscription revenue, including Apple IAP and Google Play Billing amounts, platform commissions, advertising income, and licensing fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not route mainland digital education revenue through Hong Kong as offshore turnover; the controlling economic factors such as Chinese users, servers, marketing, and payment acceptance make the revenue China-sourced; include the full gross amount before foreign platform commissions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Relevant operating costs, personnel costs, platform commissions, content licensing fees, R&D expenses, marketing, and overhead allocations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disallow non-arm's-length management fees or royalty payments to the Hong Kong partner; any related-party charge must satisfy transfer pricing documentation and the economic substance of the payee or it will be added back.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of partnership taxable income after deductions and allocation of profits to each partner under the partnership agreement in accordance with the pass-through rule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident corporate partner that is not deemed to have a PRC permanent establishment, the China-sourced passive/profit share may face 10% withholding; if the FIP constitutes a PE, the partner must self-assess at 25% on the attributable net income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declares foreign tax credits, treaty-exempt income, and reduced withholding rates claimed under the Mainland-HK Double Taxation Arrangement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For reduced treaty rates, complete the SAT treaty-relief declaration, attach the HK Tax Residency Certificate, beneficial ownership statement, partnership deed, and evidence that the Hong Kong partner has real substance; otherwise claim is denied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Mandatory schedule of all intercompany transactions among the FIP, the Hong Kong partner, and other affiliates, including software licenses, service fees, financing, and profit distributions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report transaction volume in RMB, identify the arm's-length method selected from CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, or Profit Split; failure to file when the RMB 40 million other-related-party threshold is exceeded triggers documentation penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of quarterly prepayments, final year-end tax liability, interest, and the top-up payment due at settlement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must ensure the Chinese withholding agent deposits WHT under the correct rate; if the DTA rate is used but the TRC is unavailable, the under-withheld amount will bear daily late-payment interest.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal representative, executive partner, or authorized tax filer signs the declaration confirming the accuracy and completeness of all reported income and deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The signor assumes personal responsibility for false declarations; the signature creates exposure to joint and several liability, travel blacklisting, and criminal tax evasion proceedings where fraud is identified.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers TCAL Article 62 penalties up to RMB 2,000 and up to RMB 10,000 where serious; late payment accrues daily interest of 0.05% under TCAL Article 32; intentional false declaration or concealment triggers TCAL Article 63 back taxes with a 50%-500% penalty; Criminal Law Article 201 criminal liability applies for tax fraud where evaded tax is material and more than 10% of the tax payable, with imprisonment up to 7 years for significant amounts.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory corporate income tax withholding on outbound dividends and China-sourced non-resident distributions; reduced to 5% under the Mainland-HK DTA where the beneficial owner is a Hong Kong resident company directly holding at least 25% of the capital of the distributing entity; for the FIP, the entity itself is pass-through, so a cash remittance to a non-resident partner is taxed as partnership profit allocation rather than as a formal corporate dividend.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The withholding agent or non-resident claimant must (1) obtain a Hong Kong Tax Residency Certificate from the Inland Revenue Department before the payment date; (2) file the treaty-benefit declaration through the e-Tax portal under SAT Announcement 2015 No. 60 as amended; (3) provide a beneficial ownership statement proving the Hong Kong partner is not a conduit and has the right to the income; (4) attach the FIP partnership agreement, board resolutions, payroll, premises, and core income-generating activity evidence; and (5) submit a withholding voucher with the treaty rate for tax authority recording before remittance.

stage_6.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding tax on interest is 10% and statutory withholding tax on royalties is 10%; under the Mainland-HK DTA the rate is reduced to 7% for interest and 7% for royalties. Software royalties are treated as royalties where the EdTech arrangement involves use of copyrighted software; a fully paid-up packaged software license without license-restricted use may be treated as business profit and thus subject to PRC tax only if a permanent establishment exists.
